faqs.title: Frequently asked questions
faqs.intro: Common questions about session tracking with OpenPanel.

items.question: Does OpenPanel have session replay?
items.answer: Yes. Session replay is available as an opt-in feature. Enable it by setting `sessionReplay: { enabled: true }` in your init config. When disabled, the replay script is never loaded. See the [session replay docs](/docs/session-replay) for setup and privacy options.

items.question: Do I need to set up session tracking separately?
items.answer: No. Sessions are created automatically from the events and page views you already send. There's no separate session SDK or configuration step.

items.question: How does OpenPanel define a session?
items.answer: A session starts when a user triggers their first event and ends after 30 minutes of inactivity. If the user returns after the timeout, a new session begins. This is consistent with how most analytics tools define sessions.

items.question: Can I see individual user sessions?
items.answer: Yes. You can view a user's session history, including the pages they visited and events they triggered in each session. This is available in the user profile view. If session replay is enabled, you can also play back the session.

items.question: Does session tracking require cookies?
items.answer: No. OpenPanel can run without cookies. Sessions can be tracked using a lightweight session identifier that doesn't require cookie consent. If you enable first-party cookies, session continuity improves but it's not required.
